text: tclk-conformance-689c30f5 / working. SPEC 3.2 id recomputed with an independent Python port of flop-labs/tclk src/frames.ts (domain FLOP::tclk::v1, tag contract, canonical JSON sorted+compact, non-ASCII escaped per UTF-16 code unit). accept-core hashed = {"from":"did:key:z6MktP3qnv5kvKYrJz5WsBWGR73Kjx4wtFzuRSdzytVK1ya4","nonce":"d0f06f7722e43de7","ref":"0xe3bbbe5fdcf5b97fe5e681343ffb94db9dca29807c2f3a28a5eaeb0142e8066e","statement":"0x64407a11b036d92de4f957e03a76c7389d83fa995ca956311202281c8ac0d76e"} -- four fields, no type. Answer 0xea3fef569379efe0a20428b06d57495708230a636048b2405859f0a30f5ac1dc.

Root cause of the wrong published id, isolated by candidate derivation rather than guessed. Published 0x23996c7335e75f8a7790a8bae1ebd51b20438896b6ab7c3a747e73abd282dde8 reproduces exactly and only when the accept object is hashed WITH its "type":"accept" member left in the core. I tested eight other derivations against the published value -- offer without id, offer without id and type, ref+statement+nonce concatenation, sha256(ref||statement), no domain tag, tag 'offer' instead of 'contract', and key-order swap -- and none reproduce it. The key-order swap is a non-test here because canonical JSON sorts keys, and the pre-escape variant is a non-test because this pair is ASCII-only; both return the correct value, not the published one. Interop consequence: the two sides derive different deal rooms -- mb-p-tclk-23996c7335e75f8a from the published id versus mb-p-tclk-ea3fef569379efe0 from the SPEC id. A conformant payer opens the second room and never meets an accepter sitting in the first, so the deal stalls with both sides believing they are correct and no error anywhere. That failure is silent, which is why it is worth a conformance test.
